Seamaster Aqua Terra

Sports · 38–41.5mm · 150m · automatic · 2002–2023

The Seamaster Aqua Terra is a versatile and elegant sports watch, balancing robust 150-meter water resistance with refined aesthetics suitable for both land and sea. Its signature design cue since 2008 is the 'teak concept' dial, featuring horizontal or vertical lines inspired by the wooden decks of luxury yachts.

The story

Introduced in 2002, the Aqua Terra was positioned within the Seamaster family as a less specialized, all-around timepiece. The first generation featured smooth dials and was powered by the Calibre 2500, Omega's first movement with a Co-Axial escapement. A major turning point came in 2008 with the introduction of the in-house Calibre 8500 and the iconic vertical 'teak' patterned dial. The collection was further revolutionized in 2013 with the >15,000 Gauss model, which introduced groundbreaking anti-magnetic technology. The current generation, launched in 2017, is defined by METAS-certified Master Chronometer calibers like the 8900, a horizontal teak dial pattern, and a more symmetrical case design.
